objective: Avoid per-chunk heap-string allocation in OLE2FRAME and OLEFRAME DXF payload emission.

behavior: OLE2FRAME and OLEFRAME encode each at-most-127-byte group-310 payload segment into a fixed 254-character stack buffer.
Each writer call receives a string_view limited to the populated uppercase-hex range and remains synchronous.
Chunk boundaries, field order, the trailing OLE marker, payload ownership, and sticky writer error state are unchanged.
implementation.compatibility: Internal writer implementation only; no installed API, public class layout, or DRW_Interface callback changed.

controls: Generated AC1024 ASCII/Binary controls cover OLE2FRAME and OLEFRAME with deterministic 300-byte payloads and verify exact 127/127/46-byte decoded chunk boundaries.
Controls also assert declared payload length, OLE trailer, unchanged caller payload, and a following-record sentinel.
limits: Source-level allocation avoidance is established by fixed stack buffers and the synchronous writer call; allocator counts, peak RSS, and throughput were not measured.
No full suite, peer runtime, native CAD application, external drawing, or sanitizer/fuzz campaign was run.
next_unblocked_slice: Continue auditing independent writer paths; consider consolidating bounded hex emission only if doing so preserves each caller's current error and output-order semantics.
